> The operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are displayed but not run when the vignette is built because they require project data.

# Formal representation

Step 04 derives variable domains and compatibility rules from the canonical DAG. The main outputs are `output/rules/VARDOM.dat`, `RULES.dat`, and `record_layout.csv`; `vardom.csv` and `rules_objects.rds` support inspection. SSPICE uses VOR and VXOR for logical groups and does not generate `STRUTT.dat` or `LISTE.dat`.

```{r rules}
source(file.path("scripts", "04_create_VARDOM_and_RULES.R"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path(config$rules_output_dir,
                                    c("VARDOM.dat", "RULES.dat", "record_layout.csv")))))
```

# Validate the theory

Step 05 uses the DAG, `RULES.dat`, and the item mapping to assess empirical properties of the induced Horn theory. Closure and minimality checks help determine whether formal implications reflect the intended dependencies. Sampling is governed by `n_random_closure_tests`, `max_seed_size`, and the seed in the configuration; interpret the results together with those settings.

```{r horn}
source(file.path("scripts", "05_validate_horn_theory.R"))
```

After changing the routing metadata, regenerate the DAG, domains, and rules before interpreting another validation result.
